title: Decoding 3D chromatin architecture reveals distinct enhancer classes underlying hierarchical gene regulation in prostate cancer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GEO series metadata for GSE314774 (ATAC-seq, 6 samples), GSE314775 (RNA-seq, 21 samples), GSE314776 (ChIP-seq, 24 samples) and GSE314777 (Region Capture Micro-C, 10 samples): all public since Jun 15 2026, each supplied only as a single RAW.tar of per-sample files. I did not download the tars. The Europe PMC supplementary-file request timed out (one attempt), so I could not open Table S2 (the enhancer coordinates).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 3,216 prostate cancer-specific enhancers (PCEs), which were called by integrating 201 H3K27ac ChIP-seq datasets (H3K27ac is a histone mark of active enhancers); CRISPR deletions of a handful of enhancers at one locus (chr6q24.1) in the 22Rv1 prostate cancer cell line; and the classification of those enhancers as central versus redundant.

a1_downloadable.note: All four GEO series are public, with no login (checked the metadata). The supplementary tables were not retrievable through Europe PMC.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only candidate label with many rows is 'is this region a cancer-specific enhancer', and it would have to be rebuilt from the coordinate list plus a set of negative regions we would choose ourselves. The interesting label (central versus redundant enhancer) exists for only a few deletions at a single locus.

a3_inputs_present.note: Genomic coordinates on hg38 (paper text), so DNA sequence can be pulled from the reference genome.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable for a yes/no enhancer label; the differential tables (log fold change, FDR) are standard.

a5_enough_rows.note: The perturbation experiments cover a few enhancers at one locus across 61 GEO samples. 3,216 PCEs is the paper's count, and I did not open the file to confirm it.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 GB if using peak and coordinate tables only
a6_fits_laptop.note: Processed peak files are small, but the raw tars are not size-checked.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not verified. The GEO sample counts look consistent with the experiments the paper describes.

a8_label_provenance.note: The PCE label is computed from H3K27ac signal thresholds. Predicting it from chromatin features is circular, and from sequence alone it just re-derives a peak-calling rule. The CRISPR outcomes are real measurements, but there are too few of them.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Enformer-style DNA sequence models could score these enhancers, but there is not enough label to train a head on

integration.partner_dataset: ENCODE cCREs (candidate regulatory elements) and published prostate CRISPRi enhancer screens
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Can sequence models tell 'central' enhancers inside a hub from redundant ones? This one locus cannot train or test that.

honest_claim_h3: At most: a sequence model separates H3K27ac-defined cancer-specific enhancers from background regions in prostate cell lines, which mostly restates the peak-calling rule.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use enhancer DNA sequence and 3D contact features to predict whether deleting an enhancer collapses the expression of its target genes.
plain_idea.train_on: Enhancer regions with their sequence and chromatin-contact context; only a handful of deletions were actually measured, all at one locus (exact number unknown).
plain_idea.predict: Whether an enhancer is central (its deletion drops target-gene RNA) or redundant, measured by CRISPR deletion followed by RNA-seq in 22Rv1 prostate cancer cells.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would let enhancer-targeting therapies prioritise the essential enhancers, but one locus is far too little data to learn that.

ml_idea: Classify central versus redundant enhancers from sequence and contact features. Not feasible: the measured perturbations are a few enhancers at one locus.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project failed Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct enhancers with CRISPR deletion plus RNA-seq readouts in GEO GSE314775: 21 samples, so a handful of deletions.

verdict_reason: This is a mechanistic single-locus study: the measured enhancer-perturbation outcomes cover only a few enhancers at chr6q24.1 (A5). The 3,216-enhancer list is a label computed from H3K27ac signal, so predicting it is circular (A2 and A8).
